body:
The original collector correctly holds inconsistent native controls, but the current installed workflow then needs a separate, reference-specific retention actor before owned resources can be cleaned. Can this become automatic for supported bounded native failures while keeping the scientific result unaccepted? Subissue of #33, following #49 and draft #50.

**Baseline:** #47’s original timeout/null-reward versus late-file disagreement remains held. #49 preserved the exact bytes, verified anonymous readback and performed the original exact-worker cleanup without repairing scores. Its narrowly bound reference recovery is evidence, not a general unattended interface. #50 packages generation/handoff but does not integrate this retention outcome.

**Scope:** inspect and reuse the existing retention and lifecycle code first. Build a source-bound, manifest-driven held-result sidecar with explicit publication eligibility, unchanged raw evidence, independently verified readback and the already reserved owned cleanup. Preserve the original held journal and native rewards; never accept late files, rewrite logs for grading or patch a task. Supported typed log inspection may provide a bounded inspection view, while stored bytes stay original. Unknown payloads and unresolved billing/admission retain explicit holds; do not broaden public eligibility or add a new storage platform.

**Comparison:** reuse the archived real failure before any new execution. Check byte/mode identity, negative scientific flags, source/task/agent/worker bindings, preserved public base, interruption/publication/uncertain-cleanup recovery, wrong-worker/foreign-resource rejection and inert completed replay. Report preservation/cleanup completion separately from scientific acceptance and task yield. No per-task hash whitelist or manual code edits in the operator flow.

**Status/budget:** initial source/offline work only, zero new model calls or jobs. No task repair, model/solver, regeneration, new capacity or automatic merge/release. Any justified native regression requires a new checkpoint within #33’s existing 32 CPUh/$90 operating ceiling, strictly below $100 extra; no new allowance. Keep this issue and epic open for review; detailed logs and eligible HF receipts go in comments.
